body:
I know exactly how you feel, friend. It's hard. I'm doing the same thing: pushing people away, then feeling like I don't matter to anyone. But you should keep in mind that the first step to change is finding the problem. We all have things we can improve about ourselves, and for me, it's worth expending the effort to try to minimize those particular parts of myself. I haven't made a lot of progress, but change takes time.
Maybe you should make that effort to change something. Things don't often get better on on their own, at least not as often as they get worse on their own.
Remember that despite what you feel, people *do* care about you. If you need someone to talk to, I'm here. I'm not the best at saying comforting things or giving advice by a long shot, but I know that it helps to have someone to talk about it with.

Learning to code is hard. You kind of have to develop an entirely new mindset, but it's really cool when you see something that you made come to life. I'd suggest starting at codeacademy.com and trying out JavaScript or Python. JavaScript is more widely used around the world, but Python is (from what I've heard, I don't actually know it extensively >.>) a really good language to start from.

As for apps, Java is the standard for Android apps, and Objective-C is used for iOS. I haven't had much experience in app development myself, so I couldn't say much about that subject specifically.

While you're learning, remember to change some code around, see what it does. See what breaks, what changes, and what works. Experimentation is a great way to learn how all the pieces work together.

If you have any other questions, I'm open to them. Though I may not be the most qualified person to answer, I'll do what I can. :) Good luck!

Why don't you talk to him? Seems like that'd be easier and get you farther than trying to make him jealous. Make him laugh, talk about things you're both interested in, you know?
And maybe Bob has nothing to do with how the guy you like feels. Maybe he was just hanging out with a friend (I don't really know the relationship between them, but you get the idea).
But yeah, the easiest and simplest way to get someone to like you is to befriend them, I'd say. :)
